scenes.heading: XML Format
scenes.narration: XML, or Extensible Markup Language, structures data using nested tags, and it long served as a standard for exchanging documents and configuration.

scenes.heading: Characteristics of XML
bullets: Data wrapped in descriptive opening and closing tags
Can be validated against a schema
scenes.narration: XML wraps every value in descriptive opening and closing tags, which makes it self-documenting. It supports attributes and deep nesting, so it can model complex documents. It can be validated against a schema like an XSD, enforcing structure. Its main drawback is that it is verbose, using far more characters than JSON to say the same thing.

scenes.heading: XML vs JSON
scenes.narration: XML uses tag-based markup and offers rich features like attributes and formal schema validation. JSON uses simpler key-value objects and is much lighter and more compact. For modern web APIs JSON usually wins, but XML still appears in enterprise systems and legacy integrations.

scenes.text: XML is powerful and strict but verbose; you'll meet it mostly in legacy and enterprise systems.
scenes.narration: The takeaway is that XML remains powerful and strict, but its verbosity means you will mostly encounter it in legacy and enterprise contexts.
